document.abstract: This paper describes the framework and current development status of the MPEG-7 standard by discussing its relationship to other relevant multimedia metadata standardization activities, and illustrates the relevance of the standard to the broadcast industry through the support MPEG-7 offers production and asset management by enabling new applications. An outline and the framework to support such new applications is described. Related work at Lancaster University, U. K., has developed a model for video content representation. The paper discusses how this model is being applied to the problem of automating video annotation through the use of a bi-directional approach.

authors.affiliation: E. Hartley and A. P. Parkes are with Lancaster University, Bailrigg, Lancaster, U.K.
authors.bio: Edward Hartley is a research assistant on the United Kingdom Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council funded “Automating Video Annotation” project, which is closely allied to the research area of his Ph.D. He obtained a first class honors degree in computer science in 1996. Prior to returning to academic study in 1994, he held a number of management and engineering positions in the electronics and telecommunications industries, during which he worked on a variety of defense and industrial projects over a period of 18 years. — Hartley is head of the U.K. delegation to MPEG and was host of the MPEG-7 Test and Evaluation meeting held at Lancaster University in February 1999. He is the author of several papers in the area of video content representation and a number of MPEG input documents.

authors.bio: Alan Parkes is a senior lecturer in computer science and member of the Distributed Multimedia Research Group at Lancaster University. He has conducted and supervised research into content-based representation of multimedia since 1985. He completed his Ph.D. in “An artificial intelligence approach to the conceptual representation of video images” in 1988. From 1998-1990 he was a post-doctoral research fellow studying “User-oriented content-based multimedia explanations.” — In recent years, Parkes has been awarded four EPSRC research grants concerned with manipulation of video metadata, including one to support involvement of his group in MPEG-7. He has also supervised research into Multimodal, Gestural, and Analogical Interfaces, and Adaptive Systems. He has published over 40 papers and an undergraduate text book.
authors.name: A. P. Parkes
